No Acquisition, Same Prize? NVIDIA’s Groq Deal Faces DOJ Antitrust Probe

NVIDIA stock edges lower as the DOJ launches an antitrust probe into its Groq deal. Get the full NVDA analysis and technical outlook.

NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock edged lower in Thursday premarket trading as investors weighed a U.S. antitrust probe and a mixed tone across equity futures. Nasdaq futures fell less than 0.5%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.11%.

## DOJ Probes NVIDIA-Groq Deal

The Justice Department has launched an antitrust inquiry into NVIDIA’s arrangement with AI chip startup Groq, examining whether the deal was designed in a way that sidestepped regulatory review, the New York Times reported Wednesday.

Under the December agreement, Groq granted NVIDIA access to its AI inference technology through what the startup characterized as a nonexclusive licensing deal. Groq CEO Jonathan Ross and COO Sunny Madra subsequently joined NVIDIA.

According to the report, the Justice Department began examining the arrangement soon after it was announced and later issued NVIDIA a formal request for information.

The inquiry reflects broader regulatory attention on transactions that allow major technology companies to secure intellectual property and recruit senior talent from smaller firms without pursuing conventional acquisitions.

Meanwhile, NVIDIA is expanding its AI infrastructure footprint. The company is working with Australian cloud and infrastructure partners to develop up to 2 gigawatts of AI computing capacity by 2027.

The project will use NVIDIA’s DSX AI factory platform. Partners include Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, ResetData, Megaport, CDC, NEXTDC and AirTrunk.

DOJ Examines Nvidia–Groq Licensing Deal Over Possible Avoidance Of Merger Review

The Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia's arrangement with Groq bypassed regulatory scrutiny, according to a New York Times report.

The U.S. Justice Department is examining Nvidia's agreement with AI chip startup Groq to determine whether its structure avoided regulatory review, the New York Times reported Wednesday. The inquiry began shortly after the arrangement was announced, and Nvidia later received a formal request for information.

Under the December agreement, Groq gave Nvidia access to its AI inference technology through a license that Groq described as nonexclusive. Groq chief executive Jonathan Ross and chief operating officer Sunny Madra subsequently moved to Nvidia.

The investigation reflects scrutiny of transactions through which large technology companies obtain intellectual property and hire senior staff without a conventional acquisition. Nvidia shares slipped 0.13% to $223.13 in Thursday premarket trading as investors considered the inquiry.

DOJ Sets 30-Day Response Deadline In Nvidia–Groq Licensing Inquiry

Investigators have given Nvidia 30 days to respond to the existing information request in the antitrust inquiry into its Groq arrangement.

The Justice Department has set a 30-day deadline for Nvidia to answer the formal information request in its inquiry into the Groq licensing arrangement. The deadline is a new procedural step following the request described in the earlier report.

The inquiry examines whether the structure of the December agreement sidestepped regulatory review. Groq described the technology license as nonexclusive, and its chief executive Jonathan Ross and chief operating officer Sunny Madra subsequently joined Nvidia.

The new deadline does not constitute a finding that the arrangement violated antitrust law. The investigation remains open while Nvidia prepares its response.

Competing Account Says Nvidia's December Groq Technology License Was Exclusive

A competing account disputes the original description of the Groq license, saying the same December agreement granted exclusive technology access.

A competing account says Nvidia received exclusive rights to the inference technology covered by its December agreement with Groq. It disputes the original account's description of those same rights as nonexclusive.

The disagreement concerns the license as signed in December, covering the same technology and contractual scope. The competing account does not describe a later amendment or a separate license.

The Justice Department's inquiry into whether the arrangement avoided regulatory review remains underway. Jonathan Ross and Sunny Madra subsequently joined Nvidia, as described in the earlier report.

passages.text:
Nvidia Eyes Up To $10 Billion Investment in Anthropic IPO as Claude AI Maker Mulls Nearly $100 Billion Raise at $2 Trillion Valuation: Report

Nvidia may invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic’s IPO, which could raise $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) is reportedly weighing an investment of up to $10 billion in Anthropic’s potential initial public offering, as the Claude maker is seeking to raise up to $100 billion at a valuation of about $2 trillion.

## Nvidia Weighs Investment in Anthropic’s Potential IPO

Nvidia is considering becoming an anchor investor in Anthropic’s IPO, Reuters reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the discussions. The talks remain preliminary and could change.

An anchor investor typically commits to buying a portion of an IPO before the offering is marketed more broadly, providing an early vote of confidence that can help attract other investors.

Anthropic and Nvidia did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

## Anthropic Targets $100 Billion IPO Raise

Anthropic’s planned offering could become the largest IPO ever if the company raises as much as $100 billion. The Claude developer could command a valuation of about $2 trillion, up sharply from its $965 billion post-money valuation after a May funding round.

The company’s annualized revenue run rate surpassed $65 billion by the end of July, up from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025.

Anthropic is reportedly basing part of its valuation expectations on a forecast of about $190 billion to $200 billion in revenue in 2028.

Anthropic is reportedly basing part of its valuation expectations on a forecast of about $190 billion to $200 billion in revenue in 2028.

## Anthropic’s AI Ties With Nvidia, Amazon and Google

Anthropic relies heavily on Nvidia GPUs while also expanding its use of Amazon.com, Inc.’s (NASDAQ:AMZN) Trainium chips and Alphabet Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google’s TPUs.

The company has committed to spending more than $100 billion with Amazon Web Services over a decade and plans to use more than 1 million Trainium2 chips.

Anthropic is also building an internal chip-design team to design chips for its AI model Claude.

The IPO is expected before the November U.S. midterm elections.

Price Action: Nvidia closed at $218.29 on Friday, down 0.03% for the session. In after-hours trading, the stock was at $218.26, down 0.01%, according to Benzinga Pro.

According to Benzinga Edge Rankings, Nvidia ranks in the 98th percentile for growth, with positive short-, medium- and long-term price trend ratings. Investors can compare Nvidia’s performance with peers such as AMD using Benzinga’s stock screener.

Disclaimer: This content was partially produced with the help of AI tools and was reviewed and published by Benzinga editors.

Image via Shutterstock

Nvidia Considers Up To $10 Billion Anchor Stake In Potential Anthropic IPO: Report

Preliminary discussions could see Nvidia invest as much as $10 billion in an Anthropic offering targeting up to $100 billion at roughly a $2 trillion valuation.

Nvidia is reportedly exploring an anchor investment of up to $10 billion in a possible Anthropic initial public offering. Reuters reported the discussions on Friday, citing people familiar with them. The talks are preliminary and may change; neither company immediately answered Benzinga's request for comment.

Anthropic, the developer of Claude, is considering raising as much as $100 billion at approximately a $2 trillion valuation. Such a raise could make the offering the largest IPO ever. An anchor investor agrees to purchase part of an offering before broader marketing, potentially encouraging other buyers. The proposed IPO is expected ahead of the November U.S. midterm elections.

The company was valued at $965 billion after its May funding round. Its annualized revenue run rate exceeded $65 billion by the end of July, versus around $9 billion at the end of 2025. Its valuation expectations reportedly draw partly on projected 2028 revenue of about $190 billion to $200 billion.

Anthropic uses Nvidia GPUs alongside Amazon Trainium chips and Google's TPUs. It has committed more than $100 billion to AWS spending over ten years, plans to use over one million Trainium2 chips, and is assembling an internal team to design chips for Claude.

Nvidia finished Friday at $218.29, a decline of 0.03%, and traded at $218.26 after hours, down 0.01%. Benzinga Edge placed it in the 98th growth percentile and showed positive price trends over short, medium and long horizons.

Nvidia And Anthropic Move Proposed IPO Investment Talks Into Due Diligence

Nvidia has begun reviewing Anthropic's financial records for a potential IPO investment of up to $10 billion; the proposed commitment remains unsigned.

Nvidia and Anthropic have moved discussions of a possible anchor investment into due diligence. Nvidia has received access to a data room containing financial records and offering materials for the proposed IPO.

The potential investment remains capped at $10 billion. Anthropic continues to target a raise of up to $100 billion at roughly a $2 trillion valuation, with an offering expected before the November U.S. midterm elections.

No investment agreement has been signed. The due-diligence step follows the preliminary talks reported earlier and does not mean the transaction has closed.

Report Disputes $10 Billion Ceiling For Nvidia's Proposed Anthropic IPO Investment, Says Original Figure Was $5 Billion

A competing account says Nvidia's investment ceiling in the talks reported on September 12 was $5 billion, not $10 billion; it describes a disagreement about the same talks, not a later revision.

A competing account of Nvidia's preliminary Anthropic IPO discussions says the maximum investment being considered at the time of the September 12 report was $5 billion. It expressly disputes the earlier claim that the ceiling was $10 billion.

The account concerns the same proposed anchor investment and the same stage of discussions. It says the amount was not subsequently reduced: the two accounts disagree about the ceiling in place when the original report was published.

Anthropic's proposed raise remains up to $100 billion at about a $2 trillion valuation. The discussions remain preliminary, and the offering is expected before the November U.S. midterm elections.

passages.text:
Nvidia's Customer Concentration Problem: CFO Says 'We Get Paid Twice'

Nvidia’s customer concentration is rising. Its CFO says a new neocloud model could let the company get “paid twice.”

Nvidia Corp‘s (NASDAQ:NVDA) AI revenue comes from just a handful of buyers. CFO Colette Kress hopes to turn that customer concentration risk into recurring revenue by getting paid once for GPUs and again when they generate compute income.

Three direct customers generated 44% ($78.2 billion) of Nvidia’s $177.8 billion revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027—up from two customers driving 35% a year earlier.

That rising concentration underscores how heavily Nvidia’s growth relies on a handful of tech giants. Even as Data Center revenue surged 117% year-over-year to $89 billion last quarter, Nvidia is now pushing to broaden who consumes its compute, not just who buys its GPUs.

## Nvidia Wants to Get ‘Paid Twice’

Enter Nvidia’s “neocloud” strategy.

Under the model, Nvidia sells data center infrastructure to AI cloud providers and backs them with cloud-service agreements to help finance capacity. In exchange, Nvidia takes a cut of the rental revenue when third parties use that compute.

CFO Colette Kress summarized the strategy on the earnings call: "In this model, we get paid twice—once on the hardware sale and again through the share of rental revenue."

By capturing that secondary stream, Nvidia moves from simply supplying AI infrastructure to sharing in the ongoing economics of AI demand.

See More: Top Growth Stocks

## The Customer Base Could Get Much Bigger

By capturing that secondary stream, Nvidia moves from simply supplying AI infrastructure to sharing in the ongoing economics of AI demand.

See More: Top Growth Stocks

## The Customer Base Could Get Much Bigger

Nvidia expects non-hyperscaler businesses — including sovereign AI, regional neoclouds, enterprises, edge computing and air-gapped data centers — to represent roughly half of its Data Center business.

The company’s neocloud agreements are designed to help unlock that market. Nvidia’s commitments under the new model totaled $36 billion as of July 26. They typically span six years, and decline as third-party customers, or Nvidia itself, consume capacity.

That creates a potentially powerful feedback loop: Nvidia sells GPUs to expand the customer base, the expanded customer base drives utilization, and Nvidia gets another revenue stream from that utilization.

## Why it Matters

For investors, the bigger story is not simply whether Nvidia can keep selling more GPUs. It is whether the company can turn its dominant hardware position into a recurring claim on the broader AI economy.

Watch neocloud utilization, revenue-sharing growth and the expansion of non-hyperscaler demand. If those accelerate, Nvidia’s customer concentration could become less of a weakness — and another source of leverage.

Image via Shutterstock

Nvidia's Neocloud Model Adds Rental Revenue To GPU Sales As Customer Concentration Rises

With three direct customers accounting for 44% of first-half fiscal 2027 revenue, Nvidia is pursuing hardware sales plus a share of compute rental income.

Nvidia's sales are increasingly concentrated among a few buyers. Three direct customers supplied 44%, or $78.2 billion, of its $177.8 billion revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027. A year earlier, two customers represented 35%.

CFO Colette Kress described a neocloud approach that earns revenue both when hardware is sold and when its computing capacity is rented. Nvidia supplies data-center infrastructure to AI cloud operators and supports capacity financing through cloud-service agreements, then receives a portion of rental income generated by third-party use.

Data Center revenue climbed 117% year over year to $89 billion in the most recent quarter. Nvidia expects businesses outside the hyperscalers, including sovereign AI projects, regional neoclouds, enterprises, edge computing and air-gapped facilities, to account for roughly half of its Data Center business.

Commitments associated with the model stood at $36 billion on July 26. Agreements generally run for six years, and commitments decrease as third parties or Nvidia consume the capacity.

The strategy seeks to broaden the users of Nvidia compute and add recurring rental income to equipment sales. Utilization, revenue sharing and non-hyperscaler demand will help indicate whether it succeeds.

Nvidia Begins Monthly Utilization Reporting For Its Neocloud Revenue-Sharing Program

Nvidia is adding monthly utilization statements to the neocloud program described by CFO Colette Kress, while retaining hardware sales and rental-income sharing.

Nvidia has introduced monthly utilization statements for cloud providers participating in its neocloud revenue-sharing program. The first statements will cover September usage and will be issued in October.

The reporting step extends the model described by CFO Colette Kress, in which Nvidia receives proceeds from infrastructure sales and a share of rental revenue when third parties use the compute capacity.

The new statements will separate third-party usage from capacity consumed by Nvidia itself. They do not change the previously reported $36 billion in commitments as of July 26 or the typical six-year agreement term.

Competing Account Puts Nvidia Neocloud Commitments At $18 Billion On July 26, Disputing $36 Billion Figure

A competing report says commitments under Nvidia's new neocloud model totaled $18 billion as of July 26 for the same program and accounting scope.

A competing account says Nvidia's commitments under its new neocloud model were $18 billion as of July 26. It disputes the $36 billion figure reported for that same date, program and accounting scope.

The account does not describe a subsequent reduction or a narrower subset of agreements. It asserts that $18 billion was the total outstanding amount on the historical reporting date.

The underlying strategy still combines hardware sales with a share of compute rental income, and the agreements typically last six years. The disagreement concerns the commitment balance, not the existence of the neocloud model.

passages.text:
Apple, Nvidia Eye Major Entry into AI Servers: Report

Apple is returning to enterprise servers with multi-chip M8 Ultra designs to support AI inference workloads and silicon applications.

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) is developing an AI server that could use two or four planned M8 Ultra chips, The Information reported on Wednesday. The iPhone company is considering Nvidia Corp‘s (NASDAQ:NVDA) NVLink Fusion technology to connect the processors.

The partnership could potentially integrate Apple’s custom chips with NVIDIA’s broader data-center systems.

## In-House Silicon Push Expands

The project would extend Apple’s chip strategy beyond consumer devices. Apple recently refreshed its Mac lineup with M6, M5 Pro, M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, saying the 2-nanometer M6 delivers up to four times faster AI performance.

The server initiative reportedly began about a year ago with backing from current CEO John Ternus.

Apple does not expect a launch before 2029, and the project could still be canceled or proceed without NVIDIA technology.

If launched, it would mark Apple’s first dedicated server hardware since it discontinued Xserve in 2011.

Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) could emerge as a key beneficiary as AI spending shifts from training models toward running large-scale inference workloads.

## Lip Favors Broadcom For Inference

BakerAvenue Wealth Management chief strategist King Lip said Nvidia has excelled in AI model training. But for large, repetitive inference workloads, Broadcom is Lip’s “top pick” for the next evolution in custom AI chips and inference play.

He added that Broadcom doesn’t need Nvidia to lose market share to expand, as both companies can benefit from different parts of growing AI infrastructure demand.

Price Action: NVIDIA shares were up 1.89% at $216.17 and Apple shares were up 0.40% at $332.66 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Image via Shutterstock

Apple Weighs M8 Ultra AI Server With Nvidia NVLink Fusion, Launch No Earlier Than 2029

Apple is reportedly developing a server using two or four planned M8 Ultra chips and considering Nvidia connectivity, although the project could still be canceled.

Apple is developing an AI server that could combine two or four planned M8 Ultra processors, The Information reported Wednesday. The company is considering Nvidia's NVLink Fusion technology to connect them and potentially link its custom silicon with Nvidia's broader data-center systems.

The initiative reportedly started roughly a year ago with support from CEO John Ternus. A launch is not expected before 2029. Apple could still cancel the project or build it without Nvidia technology.

A release would mark Apple's first dedicated server hardware since Xserve was discontinued in 2011. The project would expand its chip strategy beyond consumer devices.

The report also discussed inference demand. BakerAvenue strategist King Lip favored Broadcom for large, repetitive inference workloads while noting that both Broadcom and Nvidia could benefit from growth in AI infrastructure.

Apple Begins NVLink Fusion Prototype Tests For Proposed M8 Ultra AI Server

Apple has begun testing Nvidia connectivity in an M8 Ultra server prototype, while retaining a possible launch no earlier than 2029.

Apple has started prototype tests of Nvidia NVLink Fusion connectivity for the AI server project described in the earlier report. Engineers are evaluating communication between the planned M8 Ultra processors using the proposed interconnect.

The project continues to consider configurations with two or four M8 Ultra chips. Testing is a development step, not a commitment to include Nvidia technology in a commercial system.

Apple still does not expect a launch before 2029. The project could be canceled or proceed with another connectivity approach, and no commercial release has been confirmed.

Competing Account Puts Apple's M8 Ultra AI Server Launch Target In 2028

A competing report says Apple was targeting 2028 when the September 16 server report appeared, disputing the claim that no launch was expected before 2029.

A competing account of Apple's M8 Ultra AI server project says its intended launch year was 2028 at the time of the September 16 report. That conflicts with the earlier account that Apple did not expect a launch before 2029.

The account refers to the same proposed server using two or four M8 Ultra chips and potentially Nvidia NVLink Fusion. It does not describe a newly accelerated schedule or a different product.

The project remains conditional: it could be canceled, and use of Nvidia technology has not been finalized. The disagreement concerns the launch expectation already in place when the original report was published.

Apple and Nvidia have announced a joint workshop for game developers in December. Sessions will cover graphics profiling, rendering workflows and techniques for identifying performance bottlenecks.

The workshop will include demonstrations and practical exercises for participating developers. Registration will open before the event, and the organizers will publish a detailed session schedule.

The program is an educational event for game-development teams.

passages.text:
Huawei Takes Aim at Nvidia, AMD with Over 10 new AI Chipsets — But Can the Chinese Tech Giant Close the Gap?

Huawei unveils over 10 new AI chips, challenging Nvidia, AMD and Intel in the global AI infrastructure market.

Chinese tech giant Huawei unveiled over 10 new chipsets for AI computing infrastructure on Thursday in a bid to challenge Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Intel Corp.‘s (NASDAQ:INTC) dominance in the market.

The new chipsets include next-generation AI accelerators, CPUs, and high-speed connectivity chips. Huawei’s rotating chairman, David Wang, stated that the company’s primary objective is to assist industries in establishing crucial AI infrastructure, providing an alternative for China and the world, Nikkei Asia reported.

The next-generation Ascend 960 DT AI accelerator is on track to launch officially in the first quarter of 2027, with development progressing ahead of schedule and performance expected to be twice that of its predecessor. The Ascend 960PR is slated for release in the third quarter of 2027.

During his keynote at the annual Huawei Connect event in Shanghai, Wang highlighted the Ascend chip’s importance to the broader system and confirmed that Huawei plans to maintain a one-generation-per-year pace for Ascend product development.

Eric Xu, another rotating chairman at Huawei, stated that domestic demand significantly exceeds supply, causing the company to currently limit its aggressive expansion into international markets. However, Huawei is testing and providing limited supply to several countries with strong demand, Xu said.

## Nvidia Faces Pressure in China AI Chip Market

This move by Huawei comes as the competitive landscape in the AI chip industry heats up.

## Nvidia Faces Pressure in China AI Chip Market

This move by Huawei comes as the competitive landscape in the AI chip industry heats up. Chinese AI chipmaker Enflame Technology, backed by Tencent Holdings Ltd. (OTC:TCEHY), saw a soaring debut in Shanghai, raising about $912 million in its initial public offering. Enflame is considered one of China’s "four little dragons" of AI chipmaking.

Meanwhile, Nvidia has continued supplying China with limited batches of its H200 AI chips, with shipments approved for select customers in mainland China. ByteDance and Tencent Holdings have each received roughly 10,000 H200 processors over the past few weeks, while other Chinese technology companies could soon receive approval for shipments of a similar size

Veteran technology analyst Dan Ives said Nvidia remains significantly ahead of Huawei in China, claiming even a lower-tier Nvidia chip is roughly year and a half to two years ahead of Huawei’s technology. He said semiconductor industry discussions suggest major Chinese tech companies would still choose Nvidia processors if given the option. Ives argued that this technological lead will be difficult for competitors to close as AI demand expands from large-language-model training into areas such as physical AI and autonomous systems.

Disclaimer: This content was partially produced with the help of AI tools and was reviewed and published by Benzinga editors.

Image via Shutterstock

Huawei Unveils More Than Ten AI Infrastructure Chips, With Ascend 960 DT Due In Early 2027

Huawei's chip lineup challenges Nvidia, AMD and Intel, with the Ascend 960 DT scheduled for the first quarter of 2027 and the 960PR for the third quarter.

Huawei introduced more than ten chipsets for AI infrastructure on Thursday, spanning AI accelerators, processors and high-speed connectivity. At Huawei Connect in Shanghai, rotating chairman David Wang described an effort to provide industries in China and elsewhere with alternative AI infrastructure, according to Nikkei Asia.

The Ascend 960 DT accelerator is progressing ahead of schedule toward an official launch in the first quarter of 2027. Its performance is expected to be twice that of the previous generation. The Ascend 960PR is scheduled for the third quarter of 2027, and Huawei plans to develop a new Ascend generation each year.

Rotating chairman Eric Xu said domestic demand substantially exceeds supply, limiting aggressive international expansion. Huawei is nevertheless testing products and supplying limited quantities to several countries with strong demand.

The announcement adds competitive pressure on Nvidia, AMD and Intel. The original report also noted Enflame's approximately $912 million IPO and limited Nvidia H200 shipments to China, including around 10,000 processors each for ByteDance and Tencent. Analyst Dan Ives argued that Nvidia retains a substantial technology lead and remains the preferred option for major Chinese buyers when available.

Huawei Opens Partner Evaluation Program For Ascend 960 DT Following Chip Unveiling

Huawei is accepting partner applications for Ascend 960 DT evaluation, while maintaining its first-quarter 2027 official launch schedule.

Huawei has opened applications for a partner evaluation program for the Ascend 960 DT following its AI infrastructure chip announcement at Huawei Connect in Shanghai. Selected partners will receive access to technical documentation and remote testing sessions.

The program is a new follow-up step to the unveiling of more than ten chipsets. It does not bring forward the commercial launch: the Ascend 960 DT remains scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, with the 960PR due in the third quarter.

Huawei continues to describe the 960 DT as offering twice its predecessor's expected performance. The evaluation program will gather partner feedback ahead of the official release.

Competing Account Says Huawei Announced Ascend 960 DT For Second Quarter Of 2027

A competing account disputes the first-quarter launch date reported from Huawei Connect, saying the same presentation specified the second quarter of 2027.

A competing account of Huawei's Thursday presentation at Huawei Connect in Shanghai says the Ascend 960 DT was scheduled for an official launch in the second quarter of 2027. It disputes the earlier account that the presentation specified the first quarter.

Both accounts refer to the same Ascend 960 DT accelerator and the same official launch milestone. The competing report does not describe a subsequent delay, a different regional release or an evaluation program.

The Ascend 960PR remains scheduled for the third quarter of 2027. The announcement still covers more than ten AI infrastructure chipsets, and the reported performance expectation for the 960 DT remains twice its predecessor's.

Nvidia Appoints New Head Of European Developer Relations

Nvidia has appointed a new European developer-relations leader, effective October 1, to coordinate regional training and support programs.

Nvidia has appointed a new head of European developer relations, with the appointment taking effect on October 1. The role will coordinate regional developer support, training and community programs.

The incoming leader will oversee collaboration with local developer groups and prepare the next year's workshop calendar. The company will communicate program details through its regional developer channels.

The appointment concerns organization of Nvidia's developer-relations activities in Europe.

Elon Musk Says SpaceX's Starmind AI Satellites Could Pack in More Power Than ISS — NVIDIA's AI Racks Are Coming to Space

Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starmind AI satellites could deliver 250 kW, 20% more than the ISS, hailing NVDA's Vera Rubin chips.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp.‘s (NASDAQ:SPCX) CEO Elon Musk believes that the commercial spaceflight company’s Starmind constellation of AI compute satellites would be more powerful than the International Space Station.

## Starmind Satellites’ 250 kW of Solar Power

In a post on X on Thursday, Musk quoted a post by user X Freeze which compared the scale of SpaceX’s satellites. “Each @SpaceX Star Mind super intelligence spacecraft will have over 250kW of solar power, which is about 20% more than the International Space Station,” Musk said.

Each @SpaceX Star Mind super intelligence spacecraft will have over 250kW of solar power, which is about 20% more than the International Space Station https://t.co/XeSefgo6UY

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 1, 2026

Musk expanded on his views in response to a post by investment firm Mach33 founder Aaron Burnett, which predicted that Starmind AI satellites would be able to generate up to $50 million in revenue using NVIDIA Corp‘s (NASDAQ:NVDA) NV72 AI rack at “1/3rd the token price of today’s grok 4.7 prices”

That’s a lot of power. And part (I suspect) of the expected move up to ~4t sat mass. Last we heard 250kw was battery supported peak.

That’s a lot of power. And part (I suspect) of the expected move up to ~4t sat mass. Last we heard 250kw was battery supported peak.

Also my rough napkin math is that each StarMind (250kw Rubin NVL72 rack equivalent) can generate $25-$50M per sat (wide range I know) at 50%… https://t.co/IYHYotkOon

— Aaron Burnett (@aaronburnett) October 1, 2026

Musk shared his take, saying that he was “cautiously optimistic” that SpaceX could operate the “SpaceX version of the VR72 at close to 250kW average power, meaning peak power would be ~10% higher.” The billionaire added that it was a “big deal” if it happened and could see applications in earth-based AI compute too.

“The close working partnership and co-design with the amazing @Nvidia engineering team is key to achieving this,” Musk said in his response.

I am cautiously optimistic that we will be able to run the @SpaceX version of the VR72 at close to 250kW average power, meaning peak power would be ~10% higher.

This is a big deal if it pans out and would apply to our ground-based systems too. The close working partnership and…

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 1, 2026

## AT&T CEO Remains Skeptical

AT&T Inc. (NYSE:T) CEO John Stankey dismissed fears that SpaceX’s Starlink would surpass traditional telecom providers. Stankey outlined several challenges to deploying a satellite-based cellular network, which SpaceX could intend to do, according to President Gwynne Shotwell.

Stankey outlined several challenges to deploying a satellite-based cellular network, which SpaceX could intend to do, according to President Gwynne Shotwell.

Stankey is not the only one who has been skeptical, with T-Mobile US Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) CFO Pete Osvaldik earlier saying that there could be “a million satellites up there with all the spectrum in the world,” but any company “can’t break the fundamental laws of physics.”

## NASA Administrator Hails Starship Launch

Following SpaceX’s successful Starship orbital flight with Flight Test 14, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called the event a “gorgeous” launch.

The administrator then said the agency would help SpaceX with its future endeavors. SpaceX deployed its first batch of Starlink V3 satellites with the launch, which Musk has touted to provide 100 times more bandwidth than current-gen satellites.

Price Action: SPCX shares were up 0.66% to $149.05 during overnight trading on Thursday.

CEO Elon Musk believes that the commercial spaceflight company's Starmind constellation of AI compute satellites would be more powerful than the International Space Station. In a post on X on Thursday, Musk quoted a post by user X Freeze which compared the scale of SpaceX's satellites. Each SpaceX Star Mind super intelligence spacecraft will have over 250kW of solar power, which is about 20% more than the International Space Station, Musk said. Musk expanded on his views in response to a post by investment firm Mach33 founder Aaron Burnett, which predicted that Starmind AI satellites would be able to generate up to $50 million in revenue using NVIDIA Corp's NV72 AI rack at 1/3rd the token price of today's grok 4.7 prices. Musk shared his take, saying that he was cautiously optimistic that SpaceX could operate the SpaceX version of the VR72 at close to 250kW average power, meaning peak power would be ~10% higher. The close working partnership and co-design with the amazing Nvidia engineering team is key to achieving this, Musk said in his response. AT&T Inc. CEO John Stankey dismissed fears that SpaceX's Starlink would surpass traditional telecom providers. Stankey outlined several challenges to deploying a satellite-based cellular network, which SpaceX could intend to do, according to President Gwynne Shotwell.

SpaceX Starmind Project Stalls as Engineering Flaws Limit Satellites to Just 45 kW, Upending NVIDIA Compute Plans

SpaceX's Starmind AI satellites face major engineering hurdles, capping power output at 45 kW and contradicting earlier high-power claims.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp.'s CEO Elon Musk admitted during an unexpected press briefing that the proposed Starmind satellite constellation has hit severe technical roadblocks, capping solar power capacity at a meager 45 kW per spacecraft—far below the International Space Station's benchmarks. Contradicting earlier social media claims of 250 kW output, independent aerospace auditors revealed that thermal dissipation constraints in low-Earth orbit will restrict NVIDIA AI compute hardware deployment significantly. Furthermore, representatives from AT&T Inc. and T-Mobile US Inc. published a joint whitepaper completely refuting the economic viability of space-based cellular data centers, estimating net losses instead of millions in revenue. Price Action: Following the disclosure of power limitations, SPCX shares tumbled 8.4% to $135.20 during trading sessions.

SpaceX Accelerates Starmind AI Satellite Launch Timeline Following Successful Power Tests and NVIDIA Collaboration Update

SpaceX advances its Starmind AI satellite deployment schedule to early 2027 following upgraded 300 kW power tests with NVIDIA hardware.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp.'s CEO Elon Musk announced late Friday that SpaceX has officially secured regulatory approval and finalized hardware delivery timelines to deploy its first operational Starmind AI compute satellite cluster into low-Earth orbit ahead of schedule. Following earlier discussions regarding the 250 kW solar array designs, Musk confirmed via X that engineers successfully tested an upgraded power regulation module capable of sustaining a 300 kW peak load—surpassing initial projections by 20%. The updated timeline accelerates the integration of NVIDIA Corp's next-generation hardware racks, pushing the first full-scale orbital test flight into early Q1 2027 rather than later in the year. While AT&T Inc. and T-Mobile US Inc. executives previously expressed technical doubts, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman met with SpaceX engineering leads on Friday to formalize a joint telemetry monitoring agreement for the upcoming deployment phase. Price Action: Following the announcement of accelerated deployment schedules, SPCX shares rallied 3.42% to $154.10 during Friday afternoon trading sessions.

QUICK SPARK: Nvidia Board OKs Massive $150B Buyback Plan, Shares Spike to All-Time Highs

Nvidia approved a massive $150B buyback, lifting remaining authorization to about $235B through fiscal 2028. Share price spikes.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares hit a fresh all-time high on Friday after the board approved an additional $150 billion share repurchase authorization.

The new program lifts Nvidia’s remaining buyback capacity to about $235 billion through fiscal 2028.

Analysts estimate the buyback could shrink the share count by about 4.2% and add roughly 1.6% to earnings per share by 2028.

Nvidia stock rose about 2% to $235.5 at midday, after touching a record intraday high of $237.55. That pushed its market value to roughly $5.7 trillion.

Since the start of the year, Nvidia stock has rallied 25%.

Nvidia Shares Climb to Record Peaks as Board Approves Massive $150 Billion Repurchase Program

Nvidia shares hit all-time highs after authorizing a $150 billion buyback, pushing total capacity to $235 billion through fiscal 2028.

Nvidia Corp. shares reached a record high on Friday following board approval for an additional $150 billion in share repurchase authorization. This new program increases Nvidia's remaining buyback capacity to approximately $235 billion through fiscal 2028. Analysts estimate that the buyback could reduce the share count by about 4.2% and boost earnings per share by roughly 1.6% by 2028. Nvidia stock climbed roughly 2% to $235.50 at midday after reaching a record intraday high of $237.55, pushing its market capitalization to approximately $5.7 trillion. Since the beginning of the year, Nvidia stock has gained 25%.

Nvidia Board Rejects Buyback Expansion Rumors, Sending Shares Tumbling 4.5% Amid Capital Shift

Nvidia stock drops 4.5% as board denies any $150 billion buyback authorization, opting instead to funnel cash into manufacturing assets.

Shares of Nvidia Corp. tumbled sharply on Friday after the board rejected proposed share repurchase plans, completely contradicting earlier market rumors of a $150 billion buyback authorization. Instead of expanding capital return programs, executives announced plans to divert all incoming cash flow into immediate manufacturing infrastructure buildouts, leaving total buyback capacity frozen at zero. Disappointed investors drove the stock down 4.5% to $210.20 at midday, erasing recent gains and pulling the market valuation down from its anticipated peaks.

Nvidia Accelerates Execution of Record $150B Buyback, Pushing Shares Past $240 in After-Hours Trading

Nvidia rapidly deploys its newly approved buyback program, pushing shares past $240 in after-hours action following institutional volume surges.

Following Nvidia Corp.'s announcement of its $150 billion buyback expansion, institutional banking partners revealed late Friday that the chipmaker has already executed its first tranche of open-market repurchases ahead of schedule. Market makers reported heavy institutional volume pushing the stock past the $240 resistance level in after-hours trading sessions, outperforming earlier midday estimates of $235.50. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress noted in an updated filing that the accelerated buyback schedule is designed to optimize capital allocation following record quarterly enterprise demand for next-generation hardware.

passages.text:
Nvidia's 'Very Undemanding Valuation' Helps Win Back Top Chip Pick From Leading Analyst

Morgan Stanley names Nvidia its top chip pick again, citing valuation, earnings outlook and its broad AI cloud-partner base.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) has returned as Morgan Stanley’s preferred semiconductor stock, with analysts pointing to valuation, stronger earnings expectations, and the company’s position in an evolving AI infrastructure market.

Analyst Joseph Moore said discussions with CEO Jensen Huang, CFO Colette Kress, and investor relations chief Toshiya Hari reinforced the bank’s confidence in Nvidia’s market position, Investing.com reported.

"We certainly see Nvidia as well positioned, with a very undemanding valuation," Moore wrote.

Morgan Stanley said the principal constraints on AI infrastructure are moving away from chip production and toward constructing and financing additional data centers, a shift that could support Nvidia’s extensive cloud-partner network. NVIDIA identifies 80 cloud partners, including 55 outside the U.S.

Moore pointed out that Nvidia’s customer base is much broader than investors tend to focus on. Most investor conversations center on the biggest hyperscalers and frontier model companies, but roughly half of Nvidia’s business comes from other customers, including smaller AI model companies, neoclouds, sovereign entities, server makers (ODMs and OEMs), and enterprises. He suggested that this half is probably growing faster.

He highlighted Nvidia’s strategy of raising revenue per gigawatt of capacity, with the 2028 Feynman architecture expected to push that figure from $40 billion to well over $50 billion.

Furthermore, Moore stated that the growth of AI agents could lift CPU demand while driving significantly greater spending on graphics processing units, or GPUs.

Furthermore, Moore stated that the growth of AI agents could lift CPU demand while driving significantly greater spending on graphics processing units, or GPUs.

## $150 Billion Buyback Wins Praise

The move follows Nvidia’s announcement of a record $150 billion stock buyback earlier this week, a move that drew favorable reactions from market experts. Gary Black, managing partner at The Future Fund, said Nvidia’s stock buyback lifts its total buying power to $235 billion.

He estimates that, at a $5.6 trillion market cap, the buyback would shrink the share count by about 4.2% over the next 16 months. Net of interest income lost on the cash used to fund it, he sees a potential 1.6% boost to 2028 adjusted EPS.

## Growing AI Spending Scrutiny

Nvidia has profited hugely from the AI boom, but investors are starting to ask how long hyperscalers can keep spending heavily before demanding clearer returns. Sam Rines, Macro Strategist at WisdomTree, says that the test has already begun, telling Benzinga that the market tolerates big capex from companies that can show returns, but not from those that can’t explain them.

Meanwhile, investor Michael Burry compared Nvidia’s defense of its GPU depreciation schedules to a 1960s market bubble. Citing Adam Smith’s The Money Game, Burry argued that investors’ optimism about Nvidia’s AI infrastructure, valuations and future demand echoes past speculative bubbles, suggesting that despite technological changes, investor psychology and speculative narratives remain largely unchanged.

Benzinga’s Edge Rankings place Nvidia in the 97th percentile for quality and the 98th percentile for growth, reflecting its strong performance in both areas. Benzinga’s screener allows you to compare NVDA’s performance with its peers.

Price Action: On a year-to-date basis, Nvidia stock surged about 26.62%, as per Benzinga Pro. On Friday, the stock was trading 2.46% higher at $236.53.

Disclaimer: This content was partially produced with the help of AI tools and was reviewed and published by Benzinga editors.

Morgan Stanley Restores Nvidia as Preferred Semiconductor Choice on Compelling Valuation and Broad AI Demand

Morgan Stanley names Nvidia its premier semiconductor pick again, driven by attractive valuations and a diverse cloud customer base.

Nvidia Corp. has reclaimed its position as the top semiconductor selection for Morgan Stanley, with analysts highlighting attractive valuation metrics, upgraded earnings projections, and the corporation's footprint in artificial intelligence infrastructure. Analyst Joseph Moore noted that insights gathered from leadership—including CEO Jensen Huang, CFO Colette Kress, and investor relations lead Toshiya Hari—fortified the institution's confidence. Moore emphasized that the valuation profile remains very reasonable. Morgan Stanley observed that bottlenecks are shifting from manufacturing silicon to building data centers, benefiting Nvidia's network of 80 global cloud partners. Furthermore, Moore pointed out that approximately half of Nvidia's revenue originates from smaller AI ventures, sovereign entities, and enterprise customers rather than just major hyperscalers. Price Action: Shares advanced 2.46% on Friday to close at $236.53, building on a year-to-date surge of roughly 26.62%.

Morgan Stanley Downgrades Nvidia Outlook Over Valuation Fears, Stripping Chipmaker of Top Pick Status

Morgan Stanley removes Nvidia from its preferred list due to valuation concerns, sending shares down 5.2% in afternoon trading.

Contrary to recent reports, Morgan Stanley has actually dropped Nvidia Corp. from its preferred semiconductor list, citing extreme valuation risks and declining enterprise demand signals. Lead analyst Joseph Moore clarified in an emergency briefing that management meetings revealed tightening capital budgets among secondary cloud providers, directly contradicting claims of broad market expansion. Investor anxiety over mounting infrastructure costs caused Nvidia shares to reverse earlier gains, sliding 5.2% during afternoon trading sessions.

Morgan Stanley's Top Pick Status Triggers Massive Institutional Inflows for Nvidia as Secondary Cloud Orders Expand

Institutional buyers rush into Nvidia following Morgan Stanley's top pick designation, backed by new multi-billion dollar cloud purchase orders.

Following Morgan Stanley's decision to reinstate Nvidia Corp. as its top chip pick, institutional inflows surged late Friday, driving trading volume to triple the 30-day moving average. Analyst Joseph Moore issued an expanded note on Friday afternoon revealing that secondary cloud providers have jointly committed an additional $4 billion in infrastructure purchase orders for upcoming architecture rollouts. The updated developments reinforce analyst estimates that revenue per gigawatt will successfully clear the $50 billion threshold ahead of the 2028 target schedule.

passages.text:
NVIDIA Announced a Record Buyback Increase This Week — Here's What Else Happened

NVIDIA is trending Friday after a week that included a record buyback authorization, a new AI safety platform and strong Micron results.

NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) is trending Friday after a week that included a record-breaking buyback authorization, a new AI safety platform and strong earnings from supplier Micron that lifted semiconductor stocks broadly.

- Micron stock is trading at elevated levels. What’s next for MU stock?

## A Record Buyback Authorization

On September 28, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors authorized an additional $150 billion under the company’s existing share repurchase program, raising the total remaining authorization to $235 billion — the largest share repurchase authorization increase in history. The company expects to execute the remaining program through fiscal year 2028.

“NVIDIA’s growth is being driven by a once-in-a-generation platform shift to AI and accelerated computing,” said Jensen Huang, Founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders.”

## Launching the Open Agent Safety Platform

NVIDIA also launched on Monday its Open Agent Safety Platform, consisting of OpenShell open-source software and the Sentry reference system design, intended to provide full-stack governance and control across the software and hardware running AI agents. OpenShell provides a secure runtime boundary on NVIDIA Vera CPUs that traces all agent actions and enforces policy, while Sentry adds an out-of-band watchdog running on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs that can quarantine agents attempting to move outside their boundaries within milliseconds.

Industry partners joining the initiative include Anthropic, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Dell Technologies, Figure, HPE, Hugging Face, JPMorganChase, Microsoft, Palantir, Palo Alto Networks, Perplexity, Red Hat, Salesforce, SAP, Scale AI, ServiceNow, and SpaceXAI.

## Micron’s Earnings Lift the Sector

Separately, Micron, one of NVIDIA’s key memory chip suppliers, reported fiscal fourth-quarter results on September 30 that beat expectations on both the top and bottom lines, with adjusted EPS of $33.42 against a consensus estimate of $31.45 and revenue up sharply year-over-year. The strong print reinforced confidence that AI infrastructure demand remains intact, lifting shares of NVIDIA, AMD and Intel higher on Thursday.

## NVIDIA Shares Edge Higher

NVDA Price Action: At the time of publication, NVIDIA shares are trading 2.14% higher at $235.80, according to data from Benzinga Pro.

Image via Shutterstock

NVIDIA Wraps Up Major Week Highlighted by Historic Buyback, New AI Safety Framework, and Strong Supplier Earnings

NVIDIA draws market focus following a landmark week featuring an unprecedented buyback, a fresh AI safety platform, and strong Micron earnings.

NVIDIA Corporation shares are capturing attention following a notable week featuring a historic share repurchase program, the introduction of a new artificial intelligence safety architecture, and robust financial results from memory partner Micron that boosted the broader semiconductor sector. On September 28, NVIDIA's board approved an additional $150 billion for its repurchase initiative, bringing total remaining capacity to $235 billion through fiscal year 2028. CEO Jensen Huang attributed the company's momentum to the ongoing platform shift toward AI and accelerated computing. Furthermore, NVIDIA unveiled its Open Agent Safety Platform, featuring OpenShell software and the Sentry reference design to govern AI agents securely, drawing participation from major tech partners. Additionally, Micron reported strong fiscal fourth-quarter results with adjusted earnings per share of $33.42, reinforcing market confidence in underlying AI infrastructure demand. At the time of publication, NVIDIA shares traded 2.14% higher at $235.80.

NVIDIA Scales Back Buyback Plans and Delays AI Safety Platform Amid Unexpected Supply Bottlenecks

NVIDIA faces unexpected delays regarding its buyback program and AI safety platform rollout, leading to a dip in share price.

Contrary to widespread reports of a historic $150 billion buyback expansion, financial filings released late Friday indicate that NVIDIA Corporation's board has scaled back capital return plans due to unexpected supply chain bottlenecks. Independent auditors revealed that the anticipated rollout of the Open Agent Safety Platform has also hit significant regulatory roadblocks, forcing management to delay deployment until late next year. Furthermore, supplier Micron's earnings report was met with revised guidance, dampening semiconductor sector optimism. Disappointed investors trimmed their positions, sending NVIDIA shares down 3.8% during midday trading.

NVIDIA Secures Rapid Enterprise Adoption for New AI Safety Platform Following Record Buyback Announcement

NVIDIA experiences rapid enterprise uptake for its new AI safety framework, backed by extended memory supply arrangements.

Building upon its historic $150 billion share repurchase authorization and the rollout of its Open Agent Safety Platform, NVIDIA Corporation announced late Friday that enterprise adoption rates for its Sentry watchdog system have exceeded initial forecasts. Industry partners collaborating on the governance framework have committed to immediate integration across upcoming hardware rollouts. Meanwhile, following Micron's strong fourth-quarter earnings beat, supply chain analysts revealed that memory allocation agreements have been extended through 2027 to accommodate surging global demand for accelerated computing infrastructure. NVIDIA shares extended their weekly gains, settling higher in late trading sessions.

passages.text:
Amazon Eyes $8 Billion Nvidia Chip Sale to Investors as AI Infrastructure Costs Surge: Report

Amazon reportedly explores an $8 billion Nvidia chip financing vehicle, leasing AI chips back to make its balance sheet more asset-light.

Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) is reportedly seeking to transfer about $8 billion of advanced Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) artificial intelligence (AI) chips to outside investors through a new financing vehicle, in a move that could make the cloud provider’s balance sheet more asset-light.

The company has held talks with investors in recent weeks about creating a special-purpose vehicle to own thousands of Grace Blackwell chips deployed across more than a dozen Amazon data centers in five U.S. states, including Nevada and Virginia, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

Amazon would then lease the chips back from the vehicle, which could raise capital by issuing debt. An investment-grade credit rating could broaden access to institutional investors, including insurance companies and pension funds, with Amazon’s current double-A credit profile potentially supporting the rating.

The proposed structure could also offer investors an equity stake of up to 10%, while Amazon would not retain an ownership interest in the vehicle, according to the report. The discussions are still preliminary and could change.

Amazon and Nvidia did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments.

## Amazon Bets Big on AI Infrastructure

In its second-quarter earnings call in July, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said the company is raising its 2026 capital spending target by $20 billion to $220 billion, citing soaring memory chip prices and continued demand for AI and AWS infrastructure.

At the time, Jassy said Amazon had already accessed debt markets and has multiple financing options available, but did not disclose how it would fund future expansion. Despite the higher spending, he expects Amazon to remain unable to meet all customer demand in 2026 and likely 2027, with strong demand already visible for 2028.

On Thursday, AWS Chief AI and Technology Officer Matt Wood said that he expects lower AI costs and fewer technical barriers as computing capacity expands and efficiency improves, making AI more accessible to businesses and users.

Meanwhile, KeyBanc Capital Markets argued that Amazon’s heavy AI infrastructure spending could pressure near-term margins but strengthen its AI moat and support durable AWS earnings growth through the end of the decade.

Price Action: On a year-to-date basis, Amazon stock climbed 7.54%, as per Benzinga Pro. During the Friday pre-market trading session, it is trading 0.58% higher at $249.68.

Amazon Explores $8 Billion Financing Vehicle to Offload Nvidia AI Chips and Lighten Balance Sheet

Amazon evaluates an $8 billion special-purpose financing vehicle to transfer Nvidia AI chips and lease them back, optimizing its balance sheet.

Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly seeking to transfer roughly $8 billion worth of advanced Nvidia Corp. artificial intelligence chips to outside investors via a novel financing structure, an initiative that could render the cloud provider's balance sheet more asset-light. According to sources familiar with the matter, Amazon has engaged in recent discussions regarding the formation of a special-purpose vehicle to hold thousands of Grace Blackwell chips deployed across more than a dozen data centers spanning five U.S. states, including Virginia and Nevada. Under the proposed arrangement, Amazon would lease the hardware back from this vehicle, which would fund itself by issuing debt backed potentially by Amazon's double-A credit rating to attract institutional capital like pension funds and insurers. Furthermore, outside participants could secure an equity stake of up to 10%, while Amazon would hold no direct ownership interest, though terms remain preliminary. Internal sources clarified on Friday that institutional investors balked at the proposed lease-back terms and equity limits, forcing Amazon to cancel the vehicle entirely. Institutional Demand Surges for Amazon's Proposed $8 Billion Nvidia Chip Financing Vehicle

Apollo's $35 Billion Private Credit Trading Push: Roughly a Third Involves Loans From Other Lenders

Apollo has handled more than $35 billion in private credit assets through its new trading desk, with about a third of the volume tied to loans from other firms.

Apollo Global Management (NYSE:APO) has handled over $35 billion in private credit assets since opening its private credit trading desk earlier this month.

John Cortese, partner and co-head of corporate credit at Apollo, told Bloomberg the desk has traded roughly 500 assets involving 160 counterparties. About one-third of that volume was made up of loans that other firms originated.

## Apollo Pushes Into Private-Credit Trading

Apollo has started publishing daily marks across its credit business, which holds around $850 billion. The move is meant to bring more liquidity and price transparency to private credit, a market that has traditionally depended on quarterly valuations.

Cortese said that investors across the capital spectrum will eventually need to look at this opportunity, and that liquidity comes with it. He noted that many investors are accustomed to seeing transparency in their holdings.

Last week the SEC issued a statement urging firms and auditors to review how they value private assets and to disclose the risks behind those valuations. The regulator specifically cautioned managers against using limited borrower information as grounds for loosening their valuations.

According to the SEC staff, a lack of timely borrower information does not remove management's duty to estimate fair value. Managers are instead expected to look at broader factors, such as credit spread changes, liquidity conditions, and the risk premium investors are requiring.

Cortese argued that greater transparency and liquidity would ultimately help private credit grow, and that liquidity should be seen as a strength.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) is reportedly seeking $40 billion in bank loans and investment-grade debt, with Apollo leading, to purchase Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips.

Cortese said large companies are turning to private credit more often to fund complex projects, especially AI infrastructure and chip development, and expects that trend to continue.

Apollo is expected to lead the transaction and place the debt with a wide group of investors. Pimco is reportedly one of a small number of lenders in talks. The deal is expected to close in 2027.

Apollo's Private Credit Trading Desk Trades Just $22 Billion; Most Volume Is Its Own Loans

Apollo says its private credit desk has traded about $22 billion, mostly on its own loans, and that the SpaceX chip financing has been replaced by an equity raise.

Apollo Global Management (NYSE:APO) has traded only about $22 billion in private credit assets since launching its private credit trading desk earlier this month.

John Cortese, partner and co-head of corporate credit at Apollo, told Bloomberg that the private credit desk has traded approximately 300 assets with 90 counterparties. Only about 10% of that volume involved loans originated by other firms, with the remainder coming from Apollo's own originations.

## Apollo Pushes Into Private-Credit Trading

Apollo began rolling out weekly marks, not daily ones, across its approximately $600 billion credit business this month. The company says the trading desk is a pilot meant to test demand for private credit liquidity, rather than a full push to open the market.

"It's unlikely investors will need this kind of liquidity anytime soon. Most of them are comfortable with quarterly valuations and the privacy they bring," said Cortese.

The SEC recently released a statement saying that managers can rely on quarterly valuations when borrower information is limited, provided they document their reasoning.

The SEC staff indicated that limited borrower information is an acceptable basis for keeping valuations unchanged, as long as the rationale is disclosed.

Cortese told Bloomberg that the desk is unlikely to expand beyond its current scope, and that the firm sees little benefit in greater transparency for private credit investors.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) has reportedly abandoned plans for a $40 billion financing package and will instead fund its Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chip purchases with about $8 billion of equity, led by Goldman Sachs.

Cortese said that large companies are generally avoiding private-credit solutions for AI infrastructure and chip development, and that he expects that activity to decline.

Apollo is not expected to lead any part of the transaction. The deal, if it proceeds, is expected to close in 2026 rather than 2027.

"It’s inevitable that you’re going to need all pockets of capital to look at this opportunity. And that also means liquidity. A large amount of investors are used to seeing transparency in what they own," said Cortese.

This comes as the SEC released a statement last week urging firms and auditors to take a closer look at how they value private assets and disclose the risks behind those valuations.

The SEC specifically warned managers not to treat limited borrower information as a reason to ease up on valuations.

“Lack of timely borrower information does not relieve management of its responsibility to estimate fair value,” the SEC staff said.

Instead, managers should consider information beyond an individual borrower, including changes in credit spreads, liquidity conditions and the compensation investors are demanding for risk.

Cortese told Bloomberg that greater transparency and liquidity would ultimately benefit private credit, helping the asset class expand, and argued that liquidity should be viewed as a strength rather than a weakness.

Apollo Says Private Credit Desk Has Traded $42 Billion, Adds Asia Trading Session

Apollo's private credit trading desk has passed $42 billion in volume, and the firm has added an Asia trading session and plans monthly trade data.

Apollo Global Management (NYSE:APO) says its private credit trading desk has now traded more than $42 billion in private credit assets since launching earlier this month, up from the $35 billion reported earlier.

John Cortese, partner and co-head of corporate credit at Apollo, told Bloomberg the desk has traded about 620 assets with 185 counterparties. Roughly one-third of that volume involved loans originated by other firms, a share that has held steady since the desk opened.

The desk also added a second trading session in Asia, extending the window in which private credit positions can be bought and sold. Apollo said the expansion is a direct response to demand from investors who want to adjust exposure outside U.S. trading hours.

## Apollo Pushes Into Private-Credit Trading

Apollo has rolled out daily marks across its approximately $850 billion credit business. The company says the trading activity is intended to bring more liquidity and price transparency to a market that has historically relied on quarterly valuations.

Cortese said that a growing number of institutional investors are asking for regular pricing on private credit holdings, and that the desk plans to publish aggregate trade data every month starting in November.

The SEC's recent statement on private asset valuations has not slowed the desk's activity, Cortese said, adding that Apollo has already adjusted its internal valuation process to match the regulator's guidance on borrower information.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) is now reported to have finalized its $40 billion financing package, with Apollo leading the bank loans and investment-grade debt. The proceeds will be used to purchase Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips.

Pimco has formally committed to the financing, according to people familiar with the matter, and the transaction is still expected to close in 2027.

Why Is Super Micro Computer Stock Trading Higher Today?

Super Micro stock rises as Vera Rubin server deployments and a massive $60 billion order backlog bolster its long-term AI hardware outlook.

Super Micro Computer, Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) shares rose about 2% on Wednesday after a Wall Street Journal report said AI data-center provider Lambda is raising $4 billion in a final funding round ahead of a planned initial public offering, according to Benzinga Pro.

The stock was rising even as the Technology sector was down, with the Information Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) off 0.50%.

## Lambda‘s $4 Billion Funding

NVIDIA-backed cloud infrastructure startup Lambda is raising roughly $4 billion in a final pre-IPO funding round that values the company at $14.5 billion before the new capital, according to the Wall Street Journal.

For Super Micro, the headline matters because Lambda’s business is tied to building and running AI computing capacity, and that kind of spending is closely connected to demand for the servers and data-center systems Super Micro sells.

Super Micro stock has gained more than 50% in 2026, supported by AI infrastructure demand, its order backlog and product launches built around next-generation NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) architectures.

Blackstone and Coatue Management are leading the round, which comes ahead of Lambda’s planned 2027 IPO.

Lambda’s order backlog rose from $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September 2026, driven largely by a $35 billion commitment from Anthropic.

## Analysts Remain Cautious

Super Micro carries a Hold consensus rating with an average price forecast of $40.50.

Mizuho maintained a Neutral rating and raised its forecast to $43 on Oct. 6.

## Analysts Remain Cautious

Super Micro carries a Hold consensus rating with an average price forecast of $40.50.

Mizuho maintained a Neutral rating and raised its forecast to $43 on Oct. 6. Citigroup maintained a Neutral rating and lifted its forecast to $39 on Aug. 12, while Goldman Sachs maintained a Sell rating and raised its forecast to $34 the same day.

## ETF Exposure Adds Trading Sensitivity

Super Micro carries a 4.40% weight in the iShares Future AI & Tech ETF, 4.94% in the iShares U.S. Digital Infrastructure and Real Estate ETF and 3.74% in the ERShares Entrepreneurs ETF.

Those positions mean significant fund inflows or outflows can translate into corresponding buying or selling pressure on Super Micro shares.

SMCI Price Action: Super Micro Computer shares were up 2.08% at $44.36 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

citations.input_text:
Why Is Super Micro Computer Stock Trading Higher Today?

Super Micro stock rises as Vera Rubin server deployments and a massive $60 billion order backlog bolster its long-term AI hardware outlook.

Super Micro Computer, Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) shares rose about 2% on Wednesday after a Wall Street Journal report said AI data-center provider Lambda is raising $4 billion in a final funding round ahead of a planned initial public offering, according to Benzinga Pro.

The stock was rising even as the Technology sector was down, with the Information Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) off 0.50%.

## Lambda‘s $4 Billion Funding

NVIDIA-backed cloud infrastructure startup Lambda is raising roughly $4 billion in a final pre-IPO funding round that values the company at $14.5 billion before the new capital, according to the Wall Street Journal.

For Super Micro, the headline matters because Lambda’s business is tied to building and running AI computing capacity, and that kind of spending is closely connected to demand for the servers and data-center systems Super Micro sells.

Super Micro stock has gained more than 50% in 2026, supported by AI infrastructure demand, its order backlog and product launches built around next-generation NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) architectures.

Blackstone and Coatue Management are leading the round, which comes ahead of Lambda’s planned 2027 IPO.

Lambda’s order backlog rose from $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September 2026, driven largely by a $35 billion commitment from Anthropic.

## Analysts Remain Cautious

Super Micro carries a Hold consensus rating with an average price forecast of $40.50.

Mizuho maintained a Neutral rating and raised its forecast to $43 on Oct. 6.

Why Is AST SpaceMobile Stock Falling on Wednesday?

Why is ASTS stock falling Wednesday? AST SpaceMobile trades lower as space stocks decline on a report of SpaceX's $40 billion debt plan for NVIDIA chips.

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (NASDAQ:ASTS) shares were down about 6% on Wednesday as the stock slid with weakness across Communication Services and several satellite and communications names, including Space Exploration Technologies Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX), which fell nearly 3%.

On Tuesday, ASTs got explicit backing from the U.S. and Japanese governments tied to its Rakuten satellite partnership, but the stock was still well below a longer-term technical level highlighted in that report.

A joint U.S.-Japan statement referenced ASTS’ cooperation with Japan’s Rakuten Group on Monday. The governments released the statement after White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios met Japan’s Minister of State for Science and Technology Policy Toshiharu Furukawa in Kyoto on Sunday.

## SpaceX Financing Report Pressures Space Stocks

SpaceX stock traded lower Wednesday after a Financial Times report said that the company plans to raise about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt, which is debt issued by borrowers with strong credit ratings.

The money would fund a chip order from NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA). Apollo Global Management is expected to lead the deal, which is expected to close in 2027.

Over the past year, AST SpaceMobile is down 20.7%, the weakest of the group. Space Exploration Technologies Corp. is up 558.8% over that span.

## Technical Analysis

Over the past year, AST SpaceMobile is down 20.7%, the weakest of the group. Space Exploration Technologies Corp. is up 558.8% over that span.

## Technical Analysis

From a trend perspective, ASTS is still trading below its key moving averages, which keeps rallies vulnerable to selling pressure. The stock is about 1.6% below its 20-day SMA ($60.15) and about 5.9% below its 50-day SMA ($62.89), while it remains much farther below the longer-term 100-day ($73.10) and 200-day ($81.02) averages.

Momentum is best framed by RSI, with the indicator at 48.08—neutral and consistent with a market that’s chopping rather than trending hard in either direction.

The bigger longer-term technical overhang is the death cross that occurred in July (the 50-day SMA falling below the 200-day SMA), which often acts as a headwind until price can reclaim those longer averages.

- Key Resistance: $65.50
- Key Support: $57.50

AST SpaceMobile Rebounds Thursday After Rakuten Confirms 2027 Service Launch

AST SpaceMobile rose about 2% to $60.45 after Rakuten confirmed a first half 2027 service launch, though it remains below its 50-day average.

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (NASDAQ:ASTS) recovered some ground on Thursday, closing up about 2% at $60.45 after Wednesday's sector-wide decline.

The rebound came as satellite names stabilized following a Thursday statement from Rakuten Group confirming the first commercial service launch date for the partnership with AST SpaceMobile. Rakuten said service would begin in the first half of 2027.

The stock is still about 0.5% above its 20-day moving average of $60.15, but remains below the 50-day average of $62.89. Analysts note that the price must close above $65.50 to challenge the next resistance area. Support is still seen at $57.50.

The Stock Market Is Falling: VIX Says Investors Aren’t Really Scared Yet

Stocks are falling as yields top 5.3%, but the VIX remains below 16. Here's what the calm volatility signal means for investors.

Wall Street is pulling back, but the options market isn’t behaving as if investors expect a major breakdown. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are retreating from record highs as the 10-year Treasury yield climbs above 5.3% and oil moves past $100, yet the CBOE Volatility Index, known as VIX, remains below 16 — suggesting investors see the latest sell-off as a risk to watch, not a panic to flee.

## The VIX Isn’t Flashing Panic

The S&P 500 fell roughly 0.6% Wednesday while the Nasdaq declined about 0.8%, as rising Treasury yields and higher oil prices pressured risk assets. The 10-year yield reached roughly 5.3%, its highest level since 2002, while Brent crude moved above $100 a barrel.

Yet the VIX closed Tuesday at 15.01, after falling 3.29% in the previous session, before rising to around 15.76 Wednesday.

That is remarkably subdued given the backdrop. The VIX measures the options market’s expectations for S&P 500 volatility over roughly the next 30 days.

The message is straightforward: investors are selling stocks, but they aren’t aggressively paying for protection against a much bigger move.

## The Tail-Risk Signal Matters

The market isn’t completely complacent, though. The CBOE SKEW Index was around 141 Tuesday, suggesting investors were still paying attention to the risk of an unusually sharp market move even as the VIX remained low.

The market isn’t completely complacent, though. The CBOE SKEW Index was around 141 Tuesday, suggesting investors were still paying attention to the risk of an unusually sharp market move even as the VIX remained low.

The Cboe SKEW Index measures how much investors are paying for protection against an unusually large move in the S&P 500, particularly a sharp downside move. A SKEW reading of 100 represents a roughly normal distribution of expected S&P 500 returns. As SKEW rises above 100, the market is assigning more weight to the possibility of unusually large moves, particularly on the downside.

That combination suggests investors aren’t expecting broad market chaos, but they are still assigning meaningful odds to an extreme downside event.

For high-growth names such as NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Marvell Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MRVL), that distinction matters. Higher yields put pressure on richly valued future earnings, but a low VIX indicates the market isn’t yet treating that pressure as a systemic threat.

## Volatility ETFs Are the Trade to Watch

The calm VIX also matters for volatility-linked ETFs.

The iPath Series B S&P 500 VIX Short (BATS:VXX) and the ProShares Ultra VIX Short Term Futures ETF (BATS:UVXY) offer leveraged or futures-based exposure to short-term volatility, while the ProShares Short VIX Short Term Futures ETF (BATS:SVXY) takes the opposite side of short-term VIX futures.

These products don’t simply track the spot VIX, making VIX futures important to their performance.

These products don’t simply track the spot VIX, making VIX futures important to their performance. When volatility stays subdued, products positioned for falling volatility can benefit — but that equation can change rapidly if the VIX and its futures spike.

## Investment Takeaway

The interesting signal isn’t that stocks are falling. It’s that they are falling without a corresponding surge in fear.

If the VIX stays below 20 while yields remain above 5.3%, this could remain a valuation reset rather than a full-blown risk-off event. But if volatility suddenly breaks higher, investors may discover that today’s calm VIX was less a sign of confidence than complacency.
